answer: Sybil cost comes from a per-identity stake bond plus a non-transferable reputation ledger. Joining requires a deposit sized to expected epoch payout, and each clone needs its own full bond, so N identities cost N bonds. Rewards flow only to accounts whose mirror of attested history is real and independent, like an open vault of scores that cannot be forged, never to fresh keys. A farm therefore pays deposit plus yield forgone on locked capital, and a lotus-scale clone crowd shrinks per-clone payout until the attack loses money.
